gloss: to call oneself, to give one's name, to claim to be

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {名乗|なの}っていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to give one's name, to introduce oneself
definitions.explanation: To state one's own name or identity when meeting someone or in an official context.

definitions.gloss: to call oneself, to claim to be, to go by the name of
definitions.explanation: To adopt or use a particular name, title, or identity. Can imply the claim may or may not be legitimate.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}を{名乗|なの}ってください。
{警察|けいさつ}に{名乗|なの}り{出|で}た。
examples.english: I came forward to the police.

examples.japanese: {電話|でんわ}で{名乗|なの}らずに{切|き}られた。
examples.english: They hung up the phone without giving their name.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}を{名乗|なの}る{男|おとこ}が{現|あらわ}れた。
examples.english: A man claiming to be a doctor appeared.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はペンネームを{名乗|なの}っている。
examples.english: He goes by a pen name.

examples.japanese: {王|おう}の{子孫|しそん}を{名乗|なの}る{人物|じんぶつ}が{名乗|なの}り{出|で}た。
examples.english: A person claiming to be a descendant of the king came forward.

notes:
The compound {名乗|なの}り{出|で}る (to come forward, to volunteer, to step forward) is very common and has two uses: coming forward to identify oneself (to police, authorities) or volunteering for something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名乗|なの}り{出|で}る — to come forward, to volunteer
- {名前|なまえ}を{名乗|なの}る — to give one's name
- ～を{名乗|なの}る — to call oneself ~, to go by ~
- {名乗|なの}り — self-introduction (noun form)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自己紹介|じこしょうかい}する — to introduce oneself (more standard/formal)
- {称|しょう}する — to call oneself, to claim (more formal/written)
